news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一艘游轮上发生了一起汉坦病毒 暴发事件,导致三人疏散,其中两人病重。暴发 与安第斯病毒株有关,在极少数情况下可导致人传人 传播。 [news-6fbde0f81170098d]
犹他大学专家发表的一篇文章解释了汉坦病毒的症状、传播和预防,其中提到了今年早些时候阿根廷的一艘游轮 暴发。 [news-610ff5010ab732f2]
弗吉尼亚理工大学的科学家正在研究汉坦病毒如何从啮齿动物传播到人类,重点关注 跨物种溢出 传播 机制和环境因素。该研究由路易斯·埃斯科巴领导,并由国家科学基金会资助。 [news-abf38ecf0d2d6ca8]
美国国家神经疾病和中风研究所的 Avindra Nath 在《JAMA Neurology》上发表的一篇评论总结了与汉坦病毒感染 (N21) 相关的神经并发症的当前证据。 [news-24fec44e088322c0]
一名游轮乘客的安第斯病毒检测呈阳性,这是一种罕见的 汉坦病毒,可以在人与人之间传播并导致严重的呼吸道疾病。此病例引起了对汉坦病毒疫苗 的关注,特别是针对安第斯病毒,该病毒尚未在美国获得批准。 [news-9e8c81c87ee00659]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hantaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: A hantavirus outbreak occurred on a cruise ship, resulting in the evacuation of three people, two of whom were seriously ill. The outbreak is linked to the Andes virus strain, which can cause human-to-human transmission in rare cases. [news-6fbde0f81170098d]

An article explaining hantavirus symptoms, spread, and prevention by an expert at the University of Utah, with a mention of a cruise ship outbreak in Argentina earlier this year. [news-610ff5010ab732f2]

Virginia Tech scientists are researching how hantaviruses transmit from rodents to humans, focusing on spillover transmission mechanisms and environmental factors. The study is led by Luis Escobar and funded by the National Science Foundation. [news-abf38ecf0d2d6ca8]

A review published in JAMA Neurology by Avindra Nath from the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke summarizes the current evidence on neurological complications associated with hantavirus infection (N21). [news-24fec44e088322c0]

A cruise ship passenger tested positive for the Andes virus, a rare hantavirus that can spread between people and cause severe respiratory illness. This case has raised attention on hantavirus vaccines, particularly for the Andes virus, which is not yet approved in the U.S. [news-9e8c81c87ee00659]

papers.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: an emerging fatal zoonotic infection.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is a potentially fatal respiratory zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, and it is acquired mostly via inhaling aerosolized excreta from infected rodents. Over the past 30 years, HCPS has expanded beyond its initial foci, and recent events suggest a potential for spread beyond traditionally endemic regions. The disease rapidly progresses from a vague prodrome to acute cardiopulmonary failure with a high fatality rate despite optimum supportive treatment. Pathophysiology involves endothelial failure, increased vascular permeability, acute thrombocytopenia and excessive immunological responses resulting in capillary leak syndrome and cardiogenic shock. It is still hard to clinically suspect early since the prodromal symptoms are vague and mirror common viral infections and respiratory disorders. Diagnostic confirmation needs serological testing or genetic approaches, which are typically unavailable in resource-limited endemic situations, leading to considerable diagnostic delays. Management is generally supportive, with early ICU admission, judicious hydration management, mechanical breathing and cardiopulmonary support including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory patients. The recent multi-country Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in May 2026 highlights the potential for fast worldwide transmission of HCPS outside of usual endemic settings. This review summarizes the current information on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options for HCPS. We also highlight the pressing need for improved global surveillance, rapid point-of-care diagnostics, global awareness among health care workers, and ongoing development of preventive vaccines and effective antiviral therapies to address this significant public health threat.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, primarily transmitted through aerosolized rodent excreta. The review outlines the disease's rapid progression to cardiopulmonary failure, despite supportive treatment, and its pathophysiology involving endothelial damage, vascular permeability, thrombocytopenia, and immunological overreaction. It highlights the challenges in early clinical suspicion due to non-specific symptoms and the limitations in diagnostic availability in resource-limited areas. The review also emphasizes the need for improved global surveillance, point-of-care diagnostics, healthcare worker awareness, and the development of vaccines and antiviral therapies. Recent outbreaks, such as the Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in 2026, underscore the potential for HCPS to spread beyond traditional endemic regions, raising concerns about global public health preparedness.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 心肺综合征:一种新出现的致命人畜共患感染。
papers.source_body_en: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is a potentially fatal respiratory zoonotic infection caused by New World hantaviruses, and it is acquired mostly via inhaling aerosolized excreta from infected rodents. Over the past 30 years, HCPS has expanded beyond its initial foci, and recent events suggest a potential for spread beyond traditionally endemic regions. The disease rapidly progresses from a vague prodrome to acute cardiopulmonary failure with a high fatality rate despite optimum supportive treatment. Pathophysiology involves endothelial failure, increased vascular permeability, acute thrombocytopenia and excessive immunological responses resulting in capillary leak syndrome and cardiogenic shock. It is still hard to clinically suspect early since the prodromal symptoms are vague and mirror common viral infections and respiratory disorders. Diagnostic confirmation needs serological testing or genetic approaches, which are typically unavailable in resource-limited endemic situations, leading to considerable diagnostic delays. Management is generally supportive, with early ICU admission, judicious hydration management, mechanical breathing and cardiopulmonary support including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory patients. The recent multi-country Andes virus epidemic on a cruise ship in May 2026 highlights the potential for fast worldwide transmission of HCPS outside of usual endemic settings. This review summarizes the current information on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options for HCPS. We also highlight the pressing need for improved global surveillance, rapid point-of-care diagnostics, global awareness among health care workers, and ongoing development of preventive vaccines and effective antiviral therapies to address this significant public health threat.

papers.abstract: We read with interest the Comment published in The Lancet Microbe by Jason R Andrews and Isaac I Bogoch,1 who highlighted that the largest Andes virus outbreaks are driven by rare superspreading events, whereas most outbreaks undergo rapid stochastic extinction. This finding implies that widespread transmission is unlikely. We agree and note that the basic reproduction number, R0, might be lower than they estimated, further strengthening this conclusion.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是发表在《柳叶刀微生物》上的一封信,重点分析了安第斯病毒 暴发 及其 传播 特征。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者回顾了现有文献,并对基本再生数 R0 与观察到的 暴发 模式的影响进行了评论。
analysis_zh.main_results: 作者指出,基本再生数 R0 可能低于之前估计的,这进一步支持了 传播 不太可能广泛传播的结论。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强化了这样的观点,即安第斯病毒 暴发 主要是由罕见的超级传播事件驱动的,而不是持续的 传播,强调了这一见解对于理解病毒传播的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,监测 和控制策略应侧重于识别和减轻超级传播事件,这对于防止安第斯病毒大规模 暴发 至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于对现有文献的回顾,没有提供新数据,这限制了证据的强度。然而,作者对先前研究结果的同意为他们的解释提供了一定的信心。

papers.title: Vaccines for the prevention of hantavirus fevers: An overview of results and development prospects
papers.abstract: Hantavirus fevers, known as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, are natural focal diseases with a wide range of clinical manifestations. The causative agents are members of the genus Orthohantavirus , whose natural reservoirs are rodents of various species. There is currently no etiotropic therapy for these diseases. Specific prophylaxis through vaccination is available only in the DPRK, the Republic of Korea, and the People's Republic of China. An important objective is to provide the Russian and European markets with a relevant vaccine for HFRS prevention. Such a vaccine should be developed based on both time-proven approaches and the experience of modern developments. Analysis of the use of existing hantavirus vaccines and the specific features of vaccines under development, as well as assessment of the prospects for creating vaccines for HFRS prevention in the Russian Federation. All commercially available vaccine preparations are inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on the Hantaan and Seoul viruses. The effectiveness of these preparations varies, but a significant reduction in the incidence rate in regions with mass vaccination and a low incidence of adverse events have been noted. Several inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on relevant orthohantavirus strains have been developed in Russia. Some of these developments have successfully completed preclinical studies. The spectrum of hantavirus vaccine preparations under development includes subunit vaccines, vaccines based on virus-like particles (VLPs) and viral vectors, DNA vaccines, and mRNA vaccines. The primary immunogens are the surface glycoproteins Gn and Gc of hantaviruses. The closest to implementation into clinical practice are the DNA vaccines based on the Puumala and Hantaan viruses, which have undergone clinical trials (phase I). No vaccine for the prevention of hantavirus infections developed using virus-like particles (VLPs), viral vectors, or nucleic acids (DNA or mRNA) has undergone a full cycle of clinical trials or been licensed worldwide. On the contrary, well-established traditional technologies for manufacturing inactivated vaccines and their time-proven effectiveness provide a basis for their real prospects of practical application in the Russian Federation and other European countries.

papers.title_zh: 疫苗 用于预防汉坦病毒发烧:结果概述和发展前景
papers.source_body_en: Hantavirus fevers, known as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas, are natural focal diseases with a wide range of clinical manifestations. The causative agents are members of the genus Orthohantavirus , whose natural reservoirs are rodents of various species. There is currently no etiotropic therapy for these diseases. Specific prophylaxis through vaccination is available only in the DPRK, the Republic of Korea, and the People's Republic of China. An important objective is to provide the Russian and European markets with a relevant vaccine for HFRS prevention. Such a vaccine should be developed based on both time-proven approaches and the experience of modern developments. Analysis of the use of existing hantavirus vaccines and the specific features of vaccines under development, as well as assessment of the prospects for creating vaccines for HFRS prevention in the Russian Federation. All commercially available vaccine preparations are inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on the Hantaan and Seoul viruses. The effectiveness of these preparations varies, but a significant reduction in the incidence rate in regions with mass vaccination and a low incidence of adverse events have been noted. Several inactivated whole-virion vaccines based on relevant orthohantavirus strains have been developed in Russia. Some of these developments have successfully completed preclinical studies. The spectrum of hantavirus vaccine preparations under development includes subunit vaccines, vaccines based on virus-like particles (VLPs) and viral vectors, DNA vaccines, and mRNA vaccines. The primary immunogens are the surface glycoproteins Gn and Gc of hantaviruses. The closest to implementation into clinical practice are the DNA vaccines based on the Puumala and Hantaan viruses, which have undergone clinical trials (phase I). No vaccine for the prevention of hantavirus infections developed using virus-like particles (VLPs), viral vectors, or nucleic acids (DNA or mRNA) has undergone a full cycle of clinical trials or been licensed worldwide. On the contrary, well-established traditional technologies for manufacturing inactivated vaccines and their time-proven effectiveness provide a basis for their real prospects of practical application in the Russian Federation and other European countries.

papers.title: Hantavirus infection in Ukraine and the world: comparative analysis of the incidence dynamics of servicemen and civilians in peacetime and wartime
papers.abstract: Every year, about 200 thousand cases of hantavirus infection are detected at the global level, a significant number of which have a course in the form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Asia and Europe. The rapid course of the disease, the high mortality rate of its individual strains, which are mainly found in the Western Hemisphere, the lack of etiotropic pharmacotherapy and vaccination opportunities, as well as the characteristic features of the route of transmission of hantavirus disease (infection in the predominant most cases occurs as a result of contact with rodent body fluids), indicate that hantavirus infection remains a significant challenge to the health care system, which, nevertheless, is sporadic. To highlight the quantitative indicators of the incidence of hantavirus infection in Ukraine among servicemen and civilians from 2014 until now in peacetime and wartime and compare them with the dynamics of incidence in specific countries and on different continents of the world. Materials and methods. In the course of forming the results of the study, the authors resorted to the bibliographic method, the method of information synthesis, comparison and generalization. The analysis of scientific literature on the subject of the work took place in the scientometric databases Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar for the period from 2014 to the present. The value of the reliability of the approximation of the trend in the incidence of hantavirus infection among servicemen stationed in the Sumy region for the period from May to July 2025 inclusive was calculated, relative visualization was given without specifying absolute numbers, a graph of the specified trend was built, its line and equation were displayed. During 2021-2026, it is worth noting the significant spatio-temporal diversity of hantavirus incidence, which is caused by the interrelated cumulative impact of the climatic features of a particular region, the transformation of ecosystems and the level of urbanization associated with the activities of the human species. In the context of the aggregate incidence of hantavirus disease among servicemen and civilians of Ukraine for the first quarter of 2026, it should be noted that a total of 63 cases of this disease were detected, which may indicate the continuation of a rapid trend and an exponential increase in the number of registered cases for the above-mentioned nosology in 2026 (as of March 2026). The analysis of the incidence of hantavirus infection in Ukraine from 2014 to 2026 indicates a unique epidemiological transition: from a long period of latent endemicity with sporadic case registration to a sudden epidemic outbreak in 2025-2026. In 2025, as a result of hostilities and the associated cascade of environmental factors, an increase in the incidence of this disease among the civilian population was registered in Ukraine, namely, 436 cases, of which 428 cases (which is 98.16% for the specified period) were detected in the Sumy region, which provoked an increase in the incidence among the servicemen of the Armed Forces of Ukraine stationed in the specified region, in particular, from May to July 2025 inclusive. The obtained trend of incidence dynamics for the specified period is highly reliable, since its value of the reliability of the approximation R2 is 0.8621 and this value is in the range from 0.8 to 1.0.

papers.title: Climate change as an amplifier of hantavirus risk in South Asia: a neglected nexus.
papers.abstract: Hantavirus is seroepidemiologically established in South Asian human populations and rodent reservoirs, with anti-hantavirus antibodies confirmed in occupational risk groups in India, an independent association with chronic kidney disease demonstrated in Sri Lanka, and co-infection with leptospirosis identified in more than one-fifth of hospitalized leptospirosis patients. Despite this, the intersection of these findings with the region's intensifying monsoon floods, rapid urbanization, and climate-driven rodent ecology remains entirely unexamined. This letter highlights the neglected climate-hantavirus nexus, identifies structural vulnerabilities that amplify transmission risk in South Asia, and calls for integrated flood-response surveillance and One Health coordination across the region.

elements_zh.main_results: 汉坦病毒 在南亚人群和啮齿类动物 储存宿主 中得到血清流行病学证实,在印度的职业风险人群中证实了抗汉坦病毒抗体,在斯里兰卡证实了与慢性肾病的独立关联,并且在超过五分之一的住院钩端螺旋体病患者中发现了与钩端螺旋体病的合并感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为被忽视的气候与汉坦病毒关系的证据,表明环境变化可能会放大南亚的 传播 风险,并且他们强调了这种将气候因素与汉坦病毒流行病学 联系起来的观点的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要进行综合洪水应对 监测 和 One Health 协调,以应对南亚气候变化导致的汉坦病毒风险潜在增加。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the overlooked relationship between climate change and hantavirus risk in South Asia, emphasizing the need to understand how environmental changes may influence the spread of hantavirus infections.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a letter highlighting the intersection of climate change factors with hantavirus epidemiology in South Asia, focusing on human populations and rodent reservoirs in the region.
analysis_en.methods: The methods involve a review of existing seroepidemiological data on hantavirus in South Asian human populations and rodent reservoirs, identifying patterns of exposure and co-infections with other pathogens.
analysis_en.main_results: Hantavirus is seroepidemiologically established in South Asian human populations and rodent reservoirs, with anti-hantavirus antibodies confirmed in occupational risk groups in India, an independent association with chronic kidney disease demonstrated in Sri Lanka, and co-infection with leptospirosis identified in more than one-fifth of hospitalized leptospirosis patients.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence of a neglected climate-hantavirus nexus, suggesting that environmental changes may amplify transmission risks in South Asia, and they highlight the novelty of this perspective in linking climate factors to hantavirus epidemiology.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for integrated flood-response surveillance and One Health coordination to address the potential increase in hantavirus risk due to climate change in South Asia.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing data and does not present new empirical results, thus the evidence is general in nature and the confidence is moderate.

papers.title_zh: 气候变化是南亚汉坦病毒风险的放大器:一个被忽视的联系。

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantaan Virus Infection in Endothelial Cells: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Mechanistic ODE Simulations
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein–protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Druggability and literature analysis of these hubs provided 12 repurposing candidates across four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation (ODE) model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 output. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased IRF1-driven CXCL10. Our simulation showed that IFN-β combined with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral effect and CXCL10 output. A structural sensitivity analysis showed the antiviral predictions to hold under an alternative network topology, while the chemokine predictions depended on it. This computational pipeline prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 汉坦病毒引起肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒肺综合征,这两种疾病每年共同导致超过200,000例人类病例。然而,目前尚无针对抗病毒药物的特异性疗法获批。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们开发了一个用于系统药物再利用的三阶段计算框架。该研究重点关注汉坦病毒感染的人内皮细胞,并通过 I 型干扰素信号传导的常微分方程 (ODE) 模型评估药物扰动。
elements_zh.methods: 对汉坦病毒感染的人内皮细胞进行全转录组分析,显示出以干扰素途径为主的反应。STRING 蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络和复合网络中心性评分确定了 15 个中心基因,包括 ISG15、IRF1、CXCL10、STAT1 和 DDX58。这些中心的成药性和文献分析提供了四个优先级的 12 个再利用候选药物。
elements_zh.main_results: 早期 IFN-β 实现了最快的病毒清除(3.5 天),同时 CXCL10 输出减少。早期 JAK 抑制延迟清除(4.9 天)并增加 IRF1 驱动的 CXCL10。我们的模拟表明,IFN-β与抗CXCL10单克隆抗体相结合,在抗病毒药物效应和CXCL10输出之间产生了最佳平衡。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 然后,I 型干扰素信号传导的常微分方程 (ODE) 模型评估了八种药物扰动。结构敏感性分析表明,抗病毒药物 预测在替代网络拓扑下成立,而趋化因子预测则依赖于此。

papers.title_zh: 网络引导的药物再利用治疗内皮细胞汉坦病毒感染:通路分析、靶标识别和机制 ODE 模拟
papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein–protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58. Druggability and literature analysis of these hubs provided 12 repurposing candidates across four priority tiers. An ordinary differential equation (ODE) model of type I interferon signalling then evaluated eight drug perturbations. Early IFN-β achieved the fastest viral clearance (3.5 days) with reduced CXCL10 output. Early JAK inhibition delayed clearance (4.9 days) and increased IRF1-driven CXCL10. Our simulation showed that IFN-β combined with an anti-CXCL10 monoclonal antibody produced the best balance between antiviral effect and CXCL10 output. A structural sensitivity analysis showed the antiviral predictions to hold under an alternative network topology, while the chemokine predictions depended on it. This computational pipeline prioritises candidate therapies and phase-specific combinations for preclinical hantavirus studies.
papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒引起肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒肺综合征,这两种疾病每年共同导致超过200,000例人类病例。然而,目前尚无针对抗病毒药物的特异性疗法获批。在此,我们开发了一个三阶段的计算框架,用于系统性药物再利用。对汉坦病毒感染的人类内皮细胞进行全转录组分析显示,其反应主要由干扰素通路主导。通过STRING蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络和复合网络中心性评分,鉴定了15个枢纽基因,包括ISG15、IRF1、CXCL10、STAT1和DDX58。对这些枢纽基因的药物性及文献分析提供了四个优先等级中的12个再利用候选药物。随后,利用一类干扰素信号的常微分方程(ODE)模型评估了八种药物干预。早期使用IFN-β实现了最快的病毒清除(3.5天)并减少了CXCL10的输出。而早期使用JAK抑制剂则延迟了清除(4.9天)并增加了IRF1驱动的CXCL10输出。我们的模拟显示,IFN-β与抗CXCL10单克隆抗体的联合使用在抗病毒药物效应和CXCL10输出之间取得了最佳平衡。结构敏感性分析表明,抗病毒药物的预测在替代网络拓扑结构下依然成立,而趋化因子的预测则依赖于该网络拓扑结构。该计算流程为预临床汉坦病毒研究优先考虑候选疗法和阶段特异性组合。

papers.title: Transmisión interpersonal del virus Andes: revisión narrativa de la evidencia actual y sus implicaciones clínicas
papers.abstract: Los hantavirus constituyen un grupo de virus responsables de zoonosis emergentes transmitidas principalmente por roedores. El virus Andes (ANDV), endémico de Sudamérica, constituye una excepción dentro de este grupo viral debido a la evidencia de transmisión interpersonal limitada. El objetivo de esta revisión narrativa es actualizar la evidencia disponible sobre la transmisión humano-humano del ANDV y analizar sus implicaciones clínicas y epidemiológicas. Se realizó una búsqueda bibliográfica narrativa en PubMed/MEDLINE y Google Scholar, incluyendo estudios epidemiológicos, revisiones y trabajos experimentales relevantes. Los brotes descritos en Argentina y Chile, junto con estudios moleculares y modelos animales, apoyan la existencia de transmisión interpersonal en contextos de contacto estrecho y prolongado, especialmente durante fases iniciales de la enfermedad. La detección de ARN viral en saliva y secreciones respiratorias aporta plausibilidad biológica a este fenómeno. La capacidad de transmisión interpersonal del ANDV posee implicaciones relevantes para el aislamiento, el rastreo de contactos y la vigilancia epidemiológica en áreas endémicas. Hantaviruses constitute a group of viruses responsible for emerging zoonotic diseases primarily transmitted by rodents. Andes virus (ANDV), endemic to South America, is unique among hantaviruses because of evidence supporting limited person-to-person transmission. The aim of this narrative review is to summarize current evidence regarding interpersonal transmission of ANDV and its clinical and epidemiological implications. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar including epidemiological studies, reviews, and experimental reports. Outbreaks described in Argentina and Chile, together with molecular studies and animal models, support the existence of person-to-person transmission in settings involving close and prolonged contact, particularly during the early stages of disease. Detection of viral RNA in saliva and respiratory secretions provides biological plausibility for this phenomenon. The transmissibility of ANDV has relevant implications for patient isolation, contact tracing, and epidemiological surveillance in endemic regions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 PubMed/MEDLINE 和 Google Scholar 中进行了叙述性文献检索,包括流行病学研究、评论和实验报告。该研究重点关注阿根廷和智利,暴发 和分子研究支持在密切和长时间接触的环境中存在人与人之间的 传播。

papers.title_zh: 安第斯山脉病毒人际传播:实际证据和临床暗示的叙述修订
papers.source_body_en: Los hantavirus constituyen un grupo de virus responsables de zoonosis emergentes transmitidas principalmente por roedores. El virus Andes (ANDV), endémico de Sudamérica, constituye una excepción dentro de este grupo viral debido a la evidencia de transmisión interpersonal limitada. El objetivo de esta revisión narrativa es actualizar la evidencia disponible sobre la transmisión humano-humano del ANDV y analizar sus implicaciones clínicas y epidemiológicas. Se realizó una búsqueda bibliográfica narrativa en PubMed/MEDLINE y Google Scholar, incluyendo estudios epidemiológicos, revisiones y trabajos experimentales relevantes. Los brotes descritos en Argentina y Chile, junto con estudios moleculares y modelos animales, apoyan la existencia de transmisión interpersonal en contextos de contacto estrecho y prolongado, especialmente durante fases iniciales de la enfermedad. La detección de ARN viral en saliva y secreciones respiratorias aporta plausibilidad biológica a este fenómeno. La capacidad de transmisión interpersonal del ANDV posee implicaciones relevantes para el aislamiento, el rastreo de contactos y la vigilancia epidemiológica en áreas endémicas. Hantaviruses constitute a group of viruses responsible for emerging zoonotic diseases primarily transmitted by rodents. Andes virus (ANDV), endemic to South America, is unique among hantaviruses because of evidence supporting limited person-to-person transmission. The aim of this narrative review is to summarize current evidence regarding interpersonal transmission of ANDV and its clinical and epidemiological implications. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar including epidemiological studies, reviews, and experimental reports. Outbreaks described in Argentina and Chile, together with molecular studies and animal models, support the existence of person-to-person transmission in settings involving close and prolonged contact, particularly during the early stages of disease. Detection of viral RNA in saliva and respiratory secretions provides biological plausibility for this phenomenon. The transmissibility of ANDV has relevant implications for patient isolation, contact tracing, and epidemiological surveillance in endemic regions.

papers.title: Differential PCDH1 usage by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), but their cellular entry receptors have not been defined. We used replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes to compare entry by these viruses, the Old World rodent-borne Dabieshan virus and Tigray virus, and the shrew-borne Cao Bang virus and Amga virus. All six Gn/Gc complexes supported infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, with virus-specific efficiencies and kinetics. Genetic ablation of protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) reduced infection mediated by Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus Gn/Gc in human osteosarcoma and endothelial cells, whereas PCDH1 re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein comprising the first two extracellular cadherin domains. Infection was also inhibited by a soluble decoy containing the first cadherin domain, and by an antibody specific to that domain, indicating that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain mediates viral engagement. Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc-bearing rVSVs incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus and Andes virus Gn/Gc-bearing particles, even after normalization for glycoprotein abundance. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not detectably alter infection mediated by the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes. Thus, Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus use PCDH1 for efficient entry but differ in apparent receptor engagement and responses to PCDH1-directed inhibitors, whereas all six viruses are potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc-directed antibody ADI-42898.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cellular entry receptors of Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses, which are associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). The research compares these viruses with other hantaviruses, including Dabieshan, Tigray, Cao Bang, and Amga viruses, to determine their receptor usage. The authors found that Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal viruses use PCDH1 for efficient entry, as genetic ablation of PCDH1 reduced their infection in human cells, while re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein, and infection was inhibited by a decoy and an antibody targeting the first cadherin domain. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not affect the other four hantaviruses. The study highlights the differential receptor engagement of these viruses and suggests that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain is critical for their entry. These findings have implications for understanding hantavirus pathogenesis and could inform the development of targeted therapies or diagnostic tools. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, and the results may not fully reflect in vivo conditions.

papers.title: CLINICAL CASE OF SEVERE ASTRAKHAN SPOTTED FEVER
papers.abstract: Astrakhan spotted fever is an acute natural focal vector-transmitted disease of the tick-borne rickettsioses group. The Astrakhan region is highly endemic for ASF. In recent years, the incidence of ASF in the Russian Federation has declined. However, severe forms of the disease, including complicated, have recently become more common, and lethal outcomes have begun to be recorded. This article presents a clinical case of complicated Astrakhan spotted fever in a female patient arrived from the Astrakhan region. The patient had fallen ill suddenly with a fever reaching febrile levels, symptoms of intoxication syndrome, severe myalgia, and arthralgia. The patient treated independently and did not seek medical help. Due to deteriorating condition, she was hospitalized by ambulance at Infectious Clinical Hospital No. 2 of the Moscow City Health Department in the intensive care unit in severe condition on the seventh day of illness with a referral diagnosis of generalized bacterial infection. Based on clinical and epidemiological data, laboratory and instrumental studies, severe ASF was suspected. Complications included infectious toxic shock and bilateral interstitial pneumonia of unknown etiology. Differential diagnosis included generalized bacterial infection, leptospirosis, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, and neuroinfection. The diagnosis of ASF was confirmed by PCR: Rickettsia conorii ssp. caspia DNA was detected at a concentration of 106 copies/ml. In the intensive care unit, comprehensive care was administered, including infusion and transfusion support with correction of volume and electrolyte imbalances, broad-spectrum antibiotic combination therapy augmented with doxycycline 200 mg/day, administration of inotropic agents, and respiratory support. Extracorporeal detoxification methods were used, including continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration with selective endotoxin sorption (PLS-sorption), fresh frozen plasma, and platelet transfusions. On the 26th day of hospitalization, the patient was discharged in satisfactory condition under the supervision of an infectious disease specialist at her place of residence. Given the growth of domestic tourism in the Russian Federation, the risk of importing tick-borne rickettsioses to non-endemic regions remains high. This necessitates a cautious approach by general practitioners and infectious disease specialists to natural focal infections, particularly ASF.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to present a clinical case of severe Astrakhan spotted fever, highlighting the increasing prevalence of complicated forms of the disease and the need for heightened awareness among healthcare professionals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a single clinical case of Astrakhan spotted fever in a female patient who arrived from the Astrakhan region and was hospitalized in severe condition on the seventh day of illness.
analysis.methods: The diagnosis of Astrakhan spotted fever was confirmed through PCR testing, which detected Rickettsia conorii ssp. caspia DNA at a concentration of 106 copies/ml.
analysis.main_results: PCR confirmed the presence of Rickettsia conorii ssp. caspia DNA at 106 copies/ml, and the patient exhibited severe symptoms including infectious toxic shock and bilateral interstitial pneumonia of unknown etiology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this case as an example of the increasing severity of Astrakhan spotted fever, emphasizing the need for careful differential diagnosis and the potential for severe complications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of vigilance in diagnosing tick-borne rickettsioses, particularly in non-endemic regions, due to the rising risk of imported cases associated with domestic tourism.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single clinical case, which limits the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is strong given the direct confirmation of the pathogen through PCR and the detailed clinical presentation.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a clinical case of severe Astrakhan spotted fever in a female patient from the Astrakhan region. The patient was hospitalized with symptoms including fever, intoxication syndrome, severe myalgia, and arthralgia, and was initially diagnosed with generalized bacterial infection. PCR testing confirmed the presence of Rickettsia conorii ssp. caspia DNA at 106 copies/ml, leading to the diagnosis of severe Astrakhan spotted fever. The case highlights the increasing severity of the disease and the importance of considering tick-borne rickettsioses in differential diagnoses, especially in non-endemic regions. The study's findings suggest a need for heightened awareness among healthcare professionals due to the growing risk of imported cases linked to domestic tourism. While the study is limited to a single case, the evidence is strong and provides valuable insights into the clinical manifestations and diagnostic challenges of severe Astrakhan spotted fever.

papers.full_text: SummaryThis Research Topic brings together 22 contributions that showcase the breadth of mathematical and computational tools now used to understand and respond to infectious disease threats. Spanning mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis, the Research Topic addresses diseases ranging from COVID-19 and influenza to measles, mumps, and dengue. Contributions cluster around three central themes: extracting robust, decision-relevant forecasts from noisy real-time surveillance data; modeling how interventions, mobility, and connectivity shape transmission dynamics; and linking disease burden to environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system determinants. Together, these papers reinforce a unifying message: no single method suffices for every question, and the right analytical approach must be matched to the decision at hand, the data-generating process, and the practical consequences of getting the inference wrong. IntroductionInfectious diseases spread through a complex mix of factors, including pathogens, hosts, behavior, mobility, environment, health systems, and interventions, all of which interact with each other. Mathematical models and data analysis are essential tools for understanding and scientifically simulating these interactions. These approaches enable researchers to draw robust conclusions from incomplete data, formalize competing hypotheses regarding pathogen transmissions and intervention effects, and integrate diverse sources of evidence to generate forecasts and support evidence-based decision-making. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic accelerated the use of these tools on an unprecedented scale, with mathematical models informing decisions regarding lockdowns, vaccine allocations, and healthcare capacity-based planning in near real time. But the pandemic also made clear that good models need clear and evidence-based assumptions, must be tested against real data, should be checked against new data whenever possible, and must be used with an understanding of their uncertainty, not treated as perfect predictions (1–3). The challenge has only grown since: infectious-disease data are increasingly high-dimensional and multimodal, spanning genomic surveillance, mobility traces, wastewater signals, and electronic health records, while the methodological toolkit available to analyze them has expanded just as quickly, from classical compartmental models to machine learning and stochastic optimization.The Research Topic Mathematical Modeling and data analysis in infectious diseases responds to this landscape by bringing together 22 contributions spanning public health, applied mathematics, infectious-disease epidemiology, and microbial sciences. The Research Topic covers a wide range of approaches, such as mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analyses, applied across diseases including COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, dengue, and other pathogens of public health concern. Its unifying message is simple: no single method suffices for every question. Instead, the choice of method should follow from the decision at hand, the process generating the data, the observations actually available, and the consequences of incorrect inference or prediction. Robust inference and disease forecastingSeveral contributions in this Research Topic address a central challenge in infectious-disease surveillance: extracting stable, decision-relevant predictions from data that evolve in real time. Rojas-Díaz et al. propose a robust calibration framework for delayed compartmental models, employing controlled parameter initialization and time-varying parameters to fit COVID-19 incidence, intensive-care burden, and effective reproduction numbers across Chilean regions. Their work underscores practical identifiability and numerical stability as prerequisites for translating mechanistic models into tools that can be used operationally in public health decision-making.A complementary forecasting stream combines classical time-series methods with nonlinear learning. Xian et al. demonstrate that a SARIMA–k-nearest-neighbor (SARIMA-KNN) hybrid model improves prediction of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis in Chongqing, China, relative to its component models and Prophet-based comparators. Cao et al. integrated ARIMA and bidirectional long short-term memory networks through genetic-algorithm weighting, reporting improved COVID-19 forecasts for Japan with external validation in Germany. Alahmadi et al. applied seasonal-trend decomposition together with LightGBM to forecast post-pandemic influenza A in Saudi Arabia, illustrating the value of hybrid approaches when seasonal patterns are disrupted by structural change. Collectively, these studies point to an important direction for surveillance practice: hybrid models can disentangle recurrent linear or seasonal structure from irregular non-linear behavior, but their value depends on prospective evaluation and reporting forecasts alongside calibrated measures of uncertainty (3, 4).The Research Topic also moves beyond single-location time series. One contribution introduces a spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that leverages geographic and origin-destination relationships to capture both contemporaneous neighborhood effects and lagged spatial spillovers in infectious-disease prediction (Liu et al.). Taken together with the forecasting studies above, this work underscores that local incidence is shaped not only by its own history but also by connections to other places, reporting processes, and shifting epidemic regimes. Beyond spatial and temporal structure, several contributions strengthen the statistical foundations needed for infectious-disease data that are non-normal, highly skewed, or operationally heterogeneous. Gharaibeh et al. introduced a two-parameter skewed Loai distribution for positive, right-skewed data and demonstrate its competitive fit to COVID-19 mortality data. At the healthcare-facility scale, Chen and Zhou compared SARIMA, ETS, Prophet, and NNETAR models for forecasting multidrug-resistant organism infection rates, showing that model choice should reflect both forecast accuracy and residual diagnostics rather than point-error measures alone. Disease transmission, interventions, and mobilityMechanistic models offer a principled way to represent intervention timing, human behavior, and disease progression explicitly within the model structure. Babasola et al. formulated a time-delayed model for a potential human outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, explicitly incorporating incubation, vaccine deployment, vaccine-to-protection delays, vaccine acceptance, residual susceptibility, and compliance with non-pharmaceutical interventions. Their simulations illustrate why early deployment and rapid protection are critical, and why non-pharmaceutical interventions remain especially important before vaccine-induced protection takes effect. Building on this theme, Ntaimo et al. developed an integrated chance-constrained stochastic-programming model for optimal COVID-19 vaccination and intervention strategies across multiple municipalities in Gauteng, South Africa. By incorporating uncertainty in contact patterns, household transmission, age-specific susceptibility and infectivity, and multiple vaccine-effectiveness endpoints, their approach makes risk tolerance an explicit part of allocation decisions. This work exemplifies a valuable bridge between epidemic modeling and operations research: the goal is not merely to simulate an outbreak but also to identify feasible actions under uncertainty.Mobility is another recurring mechanism in this Research Topic. Drawing on cases from 294 Chinese cities, high-speed-rail records, migration data, and socioeconomic covariates, Zhang et al. found that rail connectivity was associated with early intercity dissemination of COVID-19 and that the Wuhan lockdown and transport suspensions disrupted this pathway. The importance of connectivity is echoed in a different setting: an age-structured, stochastic model of measles outbreaks in Northern British Columbia. Irvine et al. showed that inter-community mobility and school-based contact can increase outbreak probability and diminish the effectiveness of interventions, while the combined use of post-exposure prophylaxis and active case finding substantially reduces outbreak risk across scenarios.At a finer spatial scale, Chong et al. combined epidemiological analyses of high-rise residences in Singapore with computational fluid-dynamics simulations, identifying elevated risk within vertical building stacks, and showed how wind direction and cross-ventilation can shape plausible aerosol transport pathways. Together, these contributions demonstrate that interventions must be conditioned on the structure of connectivity itself: rail networks, buildings, households, and social contacts each create distinct transmission pathways that call for correspondingly tailored control measures. Saha et al. extended this perspective across successive COVID-19 waves through a model-based hypothesis-testing framework that compares competing evolutionary explanations while estimating changes in transmission, virulence, vaccination, immunity, and contact patterns. Their analysis reinforces that epidemic trajectories emerge from the coupling of pathogen evolution and human response and that the dominant mechanism driving transmission may shift as population immunity and intervention conditions evolve. Environment, disease burden, and surveillanceA substantial group of papers demonstrates both the value and the interpretive challenges of linking disease surveillance with environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system data. He et al. assessed meteorological influences on influenza incidence in Wuxi, while Yao et al. examined environmental determinants of influenza-like illness across cities in Fujian Province between 2015 and 2023. Tao et al. characterized severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome and its meteorological associations in Jiangsu Province. Extending this line of work, Guo et al. applied generalized additive and distributed lag non-linear models to identify non-linear, interacting, and delayed meteorological associations with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome on China's Jiaodong Peninsula. Hao and Yu take a broader ecological view, using provincial panel models to examine bacillary dysentery in China and link incidence to healthcare capacity, economic development, and forest coverage. Together, these studies show that contextual covariates can strengthen local early warning and risk stratification when lagged, non-linear, and place-specific effects are properly accounted for; they also call for careful interpretation, since ecological and predictive associations do not, on their own, establish causation.The Research Topic also broadens its scope from incidence to population-level burden. Luo et al. used Global Burden of Disease data to quantify trends, geographic inequalities, risk factors, and projected trajectories of childhood infectious encephalitis across Asia. Their results highlight persistent inequities, with lower socio-demographic development associated with higher disease burden, and underscore the continuing need to integrate surveillance, diagnostic capacity, perinatal care, environmental protection, and vaccination.Gong et al. similarly used Global Burden of Disease data, inequality analysis, decomposition, age-period-cohort modeling, and forecasting to characterize the global burden of infectious diseases attributable to drug use. At a more local spatial scale, Hu et al. combined spatial autocorrelation analysis, spatial error models, and Geodetector methods to identify clustered gonorrhea incidence and its interacting sociodemographic, healthcare, and environmental correlates in China. Agrawal et al. synthesized evidence from 47 studies and 61 mumps outbreaks across 21 countries, estimating a pooled attack rate of 14.5% and a pooled complication rate of 10.3%, while documenting substantial heterogeneity by setting, age, and vaccination context. Their meta-analysis underscores the importance of standardized reporting and context-sensitive interpretation in an era of waning immunity and uneven vaccine access. More broadly, burden estimation and evidence synthesis connect model outputs to the equity questions that should guide infectious-disease policy. Contributions cluster around three central themes: extracting robust, decision-relevant forecasts from noisy real-time surveillance data; modeling how interventions, mobility, and connectivity shape transmission dynamics; and linking disease burden to environmental, socioeconomic, and health-system determinants. full_text_sections.other: IntroductionInfectious diseases spread through a complex mix of factors, including pathogens, hosts, behavior, mobility, environment, health systems, and interventions, all of which interact with each other. Mathematical models and data analysis are essential tools for understanding and scientifically simulating these interactions. These approaches enable researchers to draw robust conclusions from incomplete data, formalize competing hypotheses regarding pathogen transmissions and intervention effects, and integrate diverse sources of evidence to generate forecasts and support evidence-based decision-making. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic accelerated the use of these tools on an unprecedented scale, with mathematical models informing decisions regarding lockdowns, vaccine allocations, and healthcare capacity-based planning in near real time. But the pandemic also made clear that good models need clear and evidence-based assumptions, must be tested against real data, should be checked against new data whenever possible, and must be used with an understanding of their uncertainty, not treated as perfect predictions (1–3). The challenge has only grown since: infectious-disease data are increasingly high-dimensional and multimodal, spanning genomic surveillance, mobility traces, wastewater signals, and electronic health records, while the methodological toolkit available to analyze them has expanded just as quickly, from classical compartmental models to machine learning and stochastic optimization.The Research Topic Mathematical Modeling and data analysis in infectious diseases responds to this landscape by bringing together 22 contributions spanning public health, applied mathematics, infectious-disease epidemiology, and microbial sciences. The Research Topic covers a wide range of approaches, such as mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analyses, applied across diseases including COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, dengue, and other pathogens of public health concern. Its unifying message is simple: no single method suffices for every question. Instead, the choice of method should follow from the decision at hand, the process generating the data, the observations actually available, and the consequences of incorrect inference or prediction. Robust inference and disease forecastingSeveral contributions in this Research Topic address a central challenge in infectious-disease surveillance: extracting stable, decision-relevant predictions from data that evolve in real time. Rojas-Díaz et al. propose a robust calibration framework for delayed compartmental models, employing controlled parameter initialization and time-varying parameters to fit COVID-19 incidence, intensive-care burden, and effective reproduction numbers across Chilean regions. Their work underscores practical identifiability and numerical stability as prerequisites for translating mechanistic models into tools that can be used operationally in public health decision-making.A complementary forecasting stream combines classical time-series methods with nonlinear learning. Xian et al. demonstrate that a SARIMA–k-nearest-neighbor (SARIMA-KNN) hybrid model improves prediction of acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis in Chongqing, China, relative to its component models and Prophet-based comparators. Cao et al. integrated ARIMA and bidirectional long short-term memory networks through genetic-algorithm weighting, reporting improved COVID-19 forecasts for Japan with external validation in Germany. Alahmadi et al. applied seasonal-trend decomposition together with LightGBM to forecast post-pandemic influenza A in Saudi Arabia, illustrating the value of hybrid approaches when seasonal patterns are disrupted by structural change. Collectively, these studies point to an important direction for surveillance practice: hybrid models can disentangle recurrent linear or seasonal structure from irregular non-linear behavior, but their value depends on prospective evaluation and reporting forecasts alongside calibrated measures of uncertainty (3, 4).The Research Topic also moves beyond single-location time series. One contribution introduces a spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that leverages geographic and origin-destination relationships to capture both contemporaneous neighborhood effects and lagged spatial spillovers in infectious-disease prediction (Liu et al.). Taken together with the forecasting studies above, this work underscores that local incidence is shaped not only by its own history but also by connections to other places, reporting processes, and shifting epidemic regimes. Beyond spatial and temporal structure, several contributions strengthen the statistical foundations needed for infectious-disease data that are non-normal, highly skewed, or operationally heterogeneous. Gharaibeh et al. introduced a two-parameter skewed Loai distribution for positive, right-skewed data and demonstrate its competitive fit to COVID-19 mortality data. At the healthcare-facility scale, Chen and Zhou compared SARIMA, ETS, Prophet, and NNETAR models for forecasting multidrug-resistant organism infection rates, showing that model choice should reflect both forecast accuracy and residual diagnostics rather than point-error measures alone. Disease transmission, interventions, and mobilityMechanistic models offer a principled way to represent intervention timing, human behavior, and disease progression explicitly within the model structure. Babasola et al. formulated a time-delayed model for a potential human outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, explicitly incorporating incubation, vaccine deployment, vaccine-to-protection delays, vaccine acceptance, residual susceptibility, and compliance with non-pharmaceutical interventions. Their simulations illustrate why early deployment and rapid protection are critical, and why non-pharmaceutical interventions remain especially important before vaccine-induced protection takes effect. Building on this theme, Ntaimo et al. developed an integrated chance-constrained stochastic-programming model for optimal COVID-19 vaccination and intervention strategies across multiple municipalities in Gauteng, South Africa. By incorporating uncertainty in contact patterns, household transmission, age-specific susceptibility and infectivity, and multiple vaccine-effectiveness endpoints, their approach makes risk tolerance an explicit part of allocation decisions. This work exemplifies a valuable bridge between epidemic modeling and operations research: the goal is not merely to simulate an outbreak but also to identify feasible actions under uncertainty.Mobility is another recurring mechanism in this Research Topic. Drawing on cases from 294 Chinese cities, high-speed-rail records, migration data, and socioeconomic covariates, Zhang et al. found that rail connectivity was associated with early intercity dissemination of COVID-19 and that the Wuhan lockdown and transport suspensions disrupted this pathway. The importance of connectivity is echoed in a different setting: an age-structured, stochastic model of measles outbreaks in Northern British Columbia. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the importance of mathematical modeling and data analysis in understanding infectious disease dynamics, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, which underscored the need for robust and evidence-based approaches to model transmission and inform public health decisions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial presents a collection of 22 contributions that span various methodologies and diseases, including but not limited to hantaviruses, influenza, measles, mumps, and dengue, with a focus on how these tools can be applied to infectious disease research.
analysis.methods: The editorial discusses the use of mathematical models, statistical forecasting, machine learning, stochastic optimization, computational fluid dynamics, and burden analysis to understand infectious disease interactions and inform decision-making.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that the 22 contributions demonstrate the diversity of approaches used to analyze infectious diseases, emphasizing that no single method is sufficient for all questions and that the choice of method must align with the specific decision, data-generating process, and potential consequences of errors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the integration of these tools allows for more accurate and context-specific insights into infectious disease dynamics, and they highlight the novelty of combining diverse analytical methods to address complex public health challenges.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for tailored analytical approaches in infectious disease research, particularly for hantaviruses, to improve surveillance, forecasting, and decision-making in public health contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a general overview of the research topic, with no specific data on hantaviruses or their associated syndromes, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial discusses the role of mathematical modeling and data analysis in infectious disease research, emphasizing their importance in understanding complex interactions and informing public health decisions. It highlights the diversity of methods used, including mechanistic modeling, statistical forecasting, and machine learning, and underscores the need for context-specific approaches. The editorial notes that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the use of these tools, but also revealed the necessity for clear assumptions, testing against real data, and acknowledging uncertainty. While the findings suggest the value of integrating these methods for better disease understanding and decision-making, the evidence is general and lacks specific data on hantaviruses, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

papers.title: ANALISIS KINERJA CNN DALAM KLASIFIKASI PENGGUNAAN MASKER WAJAH
papers.abstract: Penggunaan masker wajah merupakan upaya pencegahan yang krusial dalam menekan penyebaran penyakit melalui udara, termasuk penyakit zoonosis seperti Hantavirus. Namun, pemantauan kepatuhan secara manual masih menghadapi keterbatasan dari segi efektivitas dan efisiensi, sehingga diperlukan sistem pemantauan otomatis berbasis computer vision.Penelitian ini mengkaji kemampuan metode Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) dalam mengklasifikasikan pemakaian masker wajah ke dalam tiga kategori, yaitu incorrect_mask, with_mask, dan without_mask. Dataset yang digunakan adalah Face Mask Detection Dataset yang memuat 14.536 citra, dengan tahapan penelitian meliputi pre-processing, perancangan arsitektur CNN, pelatihan model, serta evaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, dan confusion matrix.Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model CNN mencapai akurasi sebesar 80,08%. Kelas incorrect_mask memperoleh performa terbaik dengan precision 94%, recall 99%, dan F1-score 96%, sedangkan kelas with_mask dan without_mask masih mengalami beberapa kesalahan klasifikasi akibat kemiripan karakteristik visualnya. Secara keseluruhan, metode CNN terbukti memiliki kemampuan yang memadai dalam klasifikasi penggunaan masker wajah dan berpotensi diterapkan sebagai sistem pemantauan kepatuhan masker secara otomatis di lingkungan publik

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the performance of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in classifying face mask usage into three categories: incorrect_mask, with_mask, and without_mask. The research highlights the critical role of face masks in preventing airborne diseases, including hantavirus, and addresses the limitations of manual monitoring. The Face Mask Detection Dataset, containing 14,536 images, was used for pre-processing, CNN architecture design, model training, and evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 80.08%, with the incorrect_mask class showing the best performance (precision 94%, recall 99%, F1-score 96%). However, the with_mask and without_mask classes experienced some classification errors due to similar visual characteristics. The authors conclude that CNN has sufficient capability for automatic mask usage monitoring in public settings, which could enhance public health efforts in preventing airborne diseases like hantavirus. The evidence is general and does not include specific limitations.

news.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain after three people evacuated - DD News
news.rss_summary_html: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain after three people evacuated  DD News
news.excerpt_original: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain after three people evacuated DD News
news.priority_tier_reason: 政府、WHO/CDC/ECDC或其他官方公共卫生来源
news.content: Feedback | Friday, October 09, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports Asian Games 2026 Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain after three people evacuated 07/05/26 | 10:25 am | hantavirus | Hantavirus-hit cruise ship Share Your browser does not support JavaScript Hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads to Spain after three people evacuated Getty - file photo A luxury cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak and marooned since Sunday off the coast of Cape Verde left for Spain on Wednesday, a Reuters witness said, after three people, two of them seriously ill, were evacuated. The MV Hondius, with nearly 150 people on board, is expected to dock in Spain’s Tenerife, in the Canary Islands, within three days, Spain’s Health Minister Monica Garcia said, adding that those still on board were not presenting any symptoms of the disease. Once in Tenerife, if they are still healthy, all non-Spanish citizens will be repatriated to their countries, Garcia told a press conference in Madrid. The 14 Spanish passengers will be quarantined in a military hospital in Madrid, she said. The duration of the quarantine will depend on when they potentially had contact with the virus, she said, adding that it has a 45-day incubation period. Three people – a Dutch couple and a German national – have died in the outbreak. A total of eight people – including a Swiss citizen who has returned home and is being treated in Zurich – are suspected to have contracted the virus, with three of them confirmed by laboratory testing, the World Health Organisation said. Argentina’s health ministry will carry out rodent trapping and analysis in the southern city of Ushuaia, the origin point of the cruise ship hit by the outbreak, it said in a statement. Officials are reconstructing the itinerary of the Dutch citizens who travelled in Argentina and Chile and later presented symptoms of hantavirus on the cruise, the statement said. No associated cases have been found in Argentina. EVACUATIONS South Africa confirmed it had identified among the victims the Andean strain of the virus that can – in rare cases – spread among humans through very close contact. Argentina’s health ministry said it would send Andes virus RNA and guidelines for diagnosis and treatment to laboratories in Spain, Senegal, South Africa, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. “This is the only (hantavirus) strain that is known to cause human-to-human transmission, but such transmission is very rare and ... only happens due to very close contact,” South Africa’s health ministry said. news.content_title: Here's what to know about hantavirus vaccines after the cruise ship outbreak
news.content: 24/7 LivePhiladelphiaPennsylvaniaNew JerseyDelaware 66° Hantavirus Here's what to know about hantavirus vaccines after the cruise ship outbreak The Andes virus, a rare type of hantavirus, has a mortality rate of about 38%. HHS said one American has tested positive for hantavirus as the plane with 18 MV Hondius passengers is headed to the U.S. ByDr. Jennifer Miao and Dr. Megan Still Monday, May 11, 2026 Share Follow 6abc on Google The recent cruise ship outbreak has put renewed attention on the Andes virus, a rare type of hantavirus that can spread between people and cause severe respiratory illness. But despite decades of research, there is still no approved vaccine in the U.S. Hantavirus exposure risk rises during activities like farming, forestry work and cleaning rodent-infested spaces. Current and future vaccines target high-risk groups rather than the general public, according to the World Health Organization. Hantaviruses spread from rodents to humans through droppings, urine, and saliva and less frequently, through bites or scratches. The Andes virus can cause a severe respiratory illness with a mortality rate of about 38% and remains the only hantavirus known to spread from person to person, with symptoms appearing anywhere from 4 to 42 days after exposure, according to the CDC. Hantavirus vaccine research has largely focused on strains found in Asia rather than the Andes virus in the Americas, Dr. Krutika Kuppalli, an infectious disease physician and adjunct associate professor at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, told ABC News. "Most of the human vaccine data come from Asia and focus on 'Old World' hantaviruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, particularly Hantaan virus and Seoul virus, rather than the 'New World' hantaviruses like Andes in the Americas," Kuppalli said. news.content_title: Hantavirus Can Cause Rare but Severe Neurological Complications, Suggests Study
news.content: USA: A review highlights that neurological manifestations of hantavirus infection are uncommon but can be severe. The authors emphasize the need for prospective clinical studies and experimental models to better understand the underlying mechanisms, identify potential therapeutic targets, and develop evidence-based guidelines for managing these neurological complications. Hantaviruses have caused multiple outbreaks worldwide and are associated with high mortality. Although they are primarily transmitted from rodents to humans, some viral species can also spread between people. While respiratory and renal complications are well recognized, neurological involvement remains less understood. In a review published in JAMA Neurology, Avindra Nath from the Section of Infections of the Nervous System at the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, National Institutes of Health, summarized the current evidence on neurological complications associated with hantavirus infection and outlined key research priorities. The main observations from the review include: Hantavirus infection is associated with two major clinical syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). In HPS, neurological complications are generally secondary to hypoxic, ischemic, or metabolic injury resulting from severe pulmonary and cardiac disease. In HFRS, patients may develop direct neurological complications, including meningoencephalitis and pituitary apoplexy, which can cause sudden vision loss and pituitary hormone dysfunction. Less common neurological manifestations include seizures, myelitis, and peripheral neuropathy. There are currently no approved antiviral therapies specifically for hantavirus infection, although several investigational antiviral agents have shown promise in preclinical studies. At present, supportive care and symptom management remain the standard treatment approach. The authors noted that current evidence is largely based on case reports, small case series, and regional studies, which may underestimate the true frequency of neurological complications. Since many infections occur in rural or resource-limited settings, cases may be underreported. They highlighted the need for prospective clinical studies with long-term follow-up to better define the natural history of neurological involvement. Further experimental research is also needed to clarify how the virus affects the nervous system, identify therapeutic targets, evaluate the possibility of persistent infection in immunocompromised individuals, and determine the appropriate role of antiviral and anti-inflammatory therapies. The review also emphasizes the importance of strengthening pandemic preparedness through collaborative research networks, standardized data and biospecimen collection protocols, and scalable clinical frameworks. In addition, healthcare professionals play a key role in providing accurate public information, reducing stigma, and promoting appropriate infection-control measures. Overall, the authors conclude that although neurological manifestations of hantavirus infection are uncommon, they can be serious. Improving the understanding of their pathophysiology and management will be critical for optimizing patient care and preparing for future outbreaks. Reference: Nath A. Neurological Manifestations of Hantavirus Infection: A Review. JAMA Neurol. Published online July 14, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2026.2437

news.content_zh: 发表在《JAMA Neurology》上的一项研究强调,汉坦病毒 感染虽然主要导致呼吸系统和肾脏并发症,但也可能导致罕见但严重的神经系统问题。该综述由国家神经疾病和中风研究所的 Avindra Nath 领导,总结了目前对这些神经系统表现的理解,其中包括脑膜脑炎和垂体中风等疾病。它指出,虽然这些并发症并不常见,但它们可能很严重,而且目前的证据仅限于 病例报告 和区域研究,可能低估了它们的真实频率。作者强调需要进行更全面的研究,包括前瞻性研究和实验模型,以阐明病毒对神经系统的影响并确定有效的 治疗。他们还呼吁加强大流行防范和更好的公众沟通,以减少耻辱并促进感染控制措施。

news.content: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 7-Oct-2026 Of mice and men: Examining how hantavirus leaps from rodent to human Virginia Tech lands a $400,000 NSF grant to decode how a virus carried by rodents infects people, and what conditions enable transmission. Grant and Award Announcement Virginia Tech Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: Luis Escobar, associate professor in the College of Natural Resources and Environment, uses molecular laboratory analysis and global data to map hantavirus transmission risks and prevent future spillover events. view more Credit: Photo by Chris Moody for Virginia Tech. Viruses that jump from wild animals to humans have caused pandemics and deadly disease outbreaks for thousands of years. Virginia Tech scientists in the College of Natural Resources and Environment are working to figure out how that happens. Understanding these processes could be a first step in creating a defense system to prevent or reduce the effects of future pandemics. Luis Escobar, associate professor in the Department of Fish and Wildlife Conservation, has received a $400,000 award from the National Science Foundation to lead a nationwide investigation into how environmental shifts and virus evolution cause hantaviruses to leap from wildlife to humans in a process termed "spillover transmission." Escobar is also a member of the Pandemic Prediction and Prevention Destination Area that funded pilot work for this NSF project. The two-year study will combine molecular laboratory analysis, advanced computational modeling, and long-term ecological data into to identify how and where hantaviruses pose the greatest threats to people. Virginia Tech is well positioned to conduct this innovative study of spillover transmission because of its computational infrastructure and its proximity to the Mountain Lake Biological Station in nearby Giles County, where researchers have found the highest rate of hantavirus infection among wild rodents. Going beyond a basic a present/absent test for hantavirus, the team will sequence rodent samples globally to map viral strains and their geographic variations. “We want to look at the global picture across sequences, so this project will study hantavirus from the micro scale in Virginia rodents to the macro scale from hantavirus reports globally,” Escobar said. “We are sequencing the virus, assessing climate and temperature fluctuations, and examining many different rodent species. That’s what makes this project unique. Rodents live across wide conditions, but spillover to humans only occurs under specific environmental conditions. We want to understand why.” Investigating a high-consequence virus In North and South America, human exposure has caused severe pulminary disease carrying a fatality rate as high as 60 percent. In Europe and Asia, different strains target the kidneys, with lower mortality rates. Inhaling microscopic airborne particles from dried rodent droppings, urine, or saliva causes most human exposure. While person-to-person spread is extremely rare globally, it has been seen with specific strains in South America. “Generally, we understand that the rodent infects the human, and most research is conducted at this interface,” Escobar said. “But we believe it is more complicated. We are in the infancy of understanding how pathogens behave in the wild.” By examining how entire animal communities, weather patterns, and viral genetics interact, researchers will analyze global genetic databases alongside samples from across North America to trace how the virus adapts. “Many steps occur before a person is infected,” Escobar said. “It could be that the virus is changing and becoming more aggressive in transmission. That does not mean it becomes more deadly; on the contrary, it may cause milder symptoms, giving infected animals or people more opportunities to spread it.” The team is focusing on four major areas: Genetic tracking: Mapping viral evolution through genetic sequencing. Wildlife networks: Examining transmission across co-occurring animal species. Environment and climate: Measuring how differences in temperature, rainfall, and air humidity affect transission. Severity mapping: Comparing genetic samples from fatal and mild human cases worldwide to pinpoint specific genetic flags linked to severe illness. The East Coast paradox: Virginia and the Southwest There is a baffling public health puzzle within the United States: Wild mice in Virginia have the highest virus rates in the nation at nearly 8 percent. Yet, human illnesses in Virginia are practically non-existent, with only one recorded case in the past 20 years. Nearly all severe human cases in the U.S. are in the arid Southwest, where a smaller percentage of wild rodents carry the virus. Researchers propose three main theories to explain the difference: Air moisture: Arid desert air allows dust-borne viral particles to circulate freely, whereas East Coast humidity keeps particles grounded. Milder strains: Virginia rodents may harbor genetic strains that are inherently less virulent to humans. Human habits: Variations in building design and outdoor activity reduce human contact with rodent waste in the East. The team will analyze tissue samples from 99 infected rodents collected at Virginia field sites, including Mountain Lake Biological Station and Blandy Experimental Farm. Using high-performance computing, researchers will sequence local strains and build regional risk maps predicting human exposure window. In collaboration with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Virginia Department of Health, the team will translate these risk maps into public health guidelines. “Ultimately, we want to show how data from the small Mountain Lake Biological Station can inform global regions facing Hantavirus cases,” Escobar said. “This two-way interaction benefits both research and application.” The grant also offers hands-on research opportunities for Virginia Tech students, who will gain experience in laboratory analysis, data management, and field sampling. Students in Escobar’s new course, Biogeography of Emerging Infectious Diseases in Chile, also will be part of the research team. news.content_zh: 由弗吉尼亚理工大学的 Luis Escobar 领导、美国国家科学基金会资助的一项为期两年的新研究正在研究汉坦病毒如何从啮齿动物传播到人类。该研究的重点是跨物种溢出 传播,结合分子分析、计算模型和生态数据来识别影响病毒传播的环境和遗传因素。该研究强调了“东海岸悖论”,即弗吉尼亚州的野生小鼠汉坦病毒感染率很高,但人类病例却很少见。研究人员将分析来自弗吉尼亚州现场(包括山湖生物站)的 99 份受感染的啮齿动物样本,并将它们与全球数据进行比较,以绘制病毒株及其地理变异图。目标是制定公共卫生指南,以减轻 传播 风险,特别是在美国西南部等地区,那里的严重人类病例更为常见。通过了解病毒在不同条件下如何适应和传播,这些发现可以帮助预测和预防未来的 暴发。

OffOn Stream on News American speaks out from cruise ship amid deadly hantavirus outbreak American passenger speaks out after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship AFP via Getty Images ByKelly McCarthy May 5, 2026, 6:54 PM An American passenger aboard a luxury cruise ship at the center of a deadly suspected hantavirus outbreak is speaking out on social media about the ongoing situation. "There's a lot of uncertainty, and that's the hardest part," passenger Jake Rosmarin said in a video posted to Instagram from the MV Hondius. "All we want right now is to feel safe, to have clarity, and to get home." Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise ship's Netherlands-based operator, said in its latest update on Monday that medical crews are working to evacuate sick passengers from the ship, which is currently anchored off Cape Verde. Rosmarin is one of 149 people onboard the ship, representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026.
